mean: to ride a wave of success

lit: a cart of fire: a budget as agonising as riding a burning cart

story.text: The phrase is the native Japanese reading of the Buddhist word kasha, the burning cart in which the wardens of hell carry sinners off to torment. Riding it is unending agony, and that agony came to stand for the constant pain of a household that cannot make ends meet.
story.source: Buddhist term kasha, the fiery cart of hell

use.how: Predicate with だ about money: 家計は火の車だ, 台所は火の車. Said of a household's or a business's finances, often wryly about one's own.

near.diff: 金欠 is a casual word for being short of cash yourself; 火の車 describes the finances of a household or business as desperately strained.

bad.en: (meant: my father went red in the face and raged like fire)

r: ひをみるよりあきらか
lit: clearer than looking at a fire: as plain as a blaze in front of your eyes

story.text: The image is traced to the Chinese Book of Documents. In the chapter Pan Geng, the king addressing his officials says, "I see it as plainly as one looks at a fire." Japanese built on this to say that something is even clearer than looking at fire.

use.how: Predicate in …のは火を見るより明らかだ, about a result or fact anyone can foresee, often a bad one: 失敗するのは火を見るより明らかだ.

near.diff: 一目瞭然 is what one glance at a chart or a room makes plain; 火を見るより明らか is mostly an outcome anyone can foresee.

lit: the wind hits hard, like a lone tree on an exposed hill taking the full force of the wind

mean: to outwit by doing the opposite of what is expected
lit: to get at the reverse side: to strike where an opponent is not guarding

lit: breaking the form: going beyond the set forms (kata) that an art or craft hands down

mean: (of a complaint) aimed at the wrong person
lit: the wrong gate: calling at the gate of a house other than the one you mean

mean: a guess that hits someone's secret exactly
lit: the bull's-eye: the black dot at the very centre of a target

story.text: In archery, zuboshi is the name of the black dot at the centre of the target, the spot every archer aims for. To hit it is to hit exactly what you aimed at, and from there the word came to mean a guess that lands squarely on what someone was trying to hide.
story.source: Japanese archery term for the centre of the target

use.how: As 図星だ (that hit home), 図星を指す (to guess someone's secret) or 図星を指される (to be found out). Said about someone's hidden feelings, motives or situation.

near.diff: 的を射る praises a remark that grasps the point of an issue; 図星 is guessing exactly what someone was hiding.

cue: Your friend insists she isn't upset, and you say, "You're jealous, aren't you?" She goes red and says nothing.
